decisions.evidence: yehallelukha323.png: the points under the word are clustered under yod, he and the first lamed (sheva, patah, sheva). I see no separate vertical stroke under the second lamed. The only vertical shape near it is the descender of the final kaf, which is part of the letter.

yamushu324.png: there is a vertical stroke under the word, to the left of the qamatz under the yod, with a visible gap between them. It sits under the right edge of the mem, not at the mem's center. The mem has no vowel below it (its vowel is the holam dot above the vav). A meteg on a narrow yod would sit just left of the qamatz, which is about this position, and a meteg on the mem would normally be centered under it. The crop doesn't show placement clearly enough to choose.

kamokha-pesha326.png: there is a qamatz under the initial kaf and a qamatz inside the final kaf, and nothing under the mem. The nearest vertical stroke is under נשׂא, in the next word, so it doesn't belong to כמוך.

kamokha-pesha326.png: there is a vertical stroke right next to the left of the segol under the pe, inside the pe's width. The patah under the shin is separate, further left. The stroke is clear of עַל־, which is on the other side of the maqaf.

mimei326-full.png, all lower points included: I see a hiriq dot under the first (rightmost) mem and a tsere under the second mem. A vertical stroke appears under the word, but I can't place it confidently: it could be just left of the hiriq (first mem) or next to the tsere (second mem). The vertical stroke under לאבתינו, near its tsere/hataf area, is a separate mark in that word and is not counted here.
